summary.headline: R Systems Q2 CY26 revenue rose 4.7% QoQ to Rs 601.7 crore ($63.6M) with adjusted EBITDA margin at a record 20.1%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 30.2% YoY in rupees and 17.7% in dollars, with 1.2% QoQ dollar growth, aided by rupee depreciation and the Novigo acquisition. Adjusted EBITDA reached Rs 120.7 crore (20.1% margin), but adjusted PAT fell 17.1% QoQ to Rs 62.9 crore because Q1 included a one-time hedge-accounting benefit of about Rs 18 crore. Management pointed to higher sales and marketing spend and a wage hike cycle, and declined to give numerical guidance. Constant-currency organic growth remained muted, and management argued that ACV bookings and pipeline quality would convert into revenue in the second half.

segments.name: Geography: APAC
segments.commentary: Fell to 15.3% as larger projects in the prior quarter ended.

segments.name: Geography: Europe / MEA
segments.commentary: Europe at 9.7% and Middle East and Africa at 3.6%, both broadly flat.

guidance_outlook: Management does not provide formal guidance.
Sustainable adjusted EBITDA band of 18-19%, with excess margin reinvested in AI, sales and marketing.
Constant-currency growth of 3-4% is tracked, though management said it could slip to about 2% when decisions are delayed.
Wins in H1 are expected to convert to revenue in H2; sales and marketing spend is intended to build ACV wins for the following half.
No quantified deal-win guidance; deal wins will continue to be reported on a trailing 12-month basis.
capex_capacity: Utilization 80.5-81%, which management said is the target band; bench investments made over the last 2-3 quarters are now being deployed to revenue-generating work.
Headcount broadly flat YoY despite the 18% QoQ revenue growth; productivity gains attributed to AI-led delivery (EXIQO AI Studio cited at about 2x productivity and 55% faster turnaround).
Biannual wage hike cycle; first cycle implemented in Q2 and already in the reported margins.
Novigo acquisition integrated by end of Q4 CY25 and fully consolidated in Q1 CY26.
demand_pricing: Trailing-12-month ACV bookings $82.9 million in Q2 vs $82.3 million in Q1, roughly flat.

Q2 wins included a global telecom analytics deal, a small-business lender GCC set-up in India, a BFSI AI quality-engineering win, a market-access firm's Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM programme, and an ad-tech platform modernisation.
Data, AI and cloud now above 50% of revenue (no explicit figure given).
Management says it does not face AI-driven price deflation because AI productivity is built into bids and multi-year renewal contracts are not common.
Billed DSO about 55-56 days; billed plus unbilled about 75 days.
Novigo faces a Middle East geopolitical headwind but is winning deals across markets, including the Middle East.
Wallet share has risen in top-50 clients, mainly in BFSI through AI business operations.
GCC revenue share not disclosed; management described GCC as a growth vector.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SG&A rise about USD 2M QoQ, and is there added sales hiring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a Chief Revenue Officer hire, more sales bandwidth, AI and domain experts in sales, and marketing spend around the EXIQO brand launch, with the investment described as deliberate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year organic growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. Management said trailing-12-month numbers are positive, H1 bookings flow into H2 revenue, and the company is confident in its momentum.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ACV flat QoQ in Q2 after a strong Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TTM wins are at least as high as before and Q2 had a few large deals that offset a large Q2 last year, with pipeline quality improving.

qa_highlights.question: Is Novigo adding to growth and how is its order flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Novigo integration added inorganic growth through Q1 CY26. Management said Novigo's earlier organic cliff is now matched, and it is winning deals including in the Middle East.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wage hike and near-term margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: A biannual wage hike was implemented in Q2 and is already in the numbers. Management reiterated an 18-19% sustainable adjusted EBITDA band, with FX a non-controllable tailwind.

qa_highlights.question: When will CC growth return to 3-4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said decision delays drive the timing; it expects consistent growth as the pipeline converts, but gave no date.

risks_watch: Adjusted PAT down 17.1% QoQ on the Q1 one-time hedge benefit of about Rs 18 crore; quality of earnings depends on rupee moves.
Q2 forward-cover book of $43.32 million at an average rate of 93.27; realised hedge loss of Rs 9 crore and exchange loss of Rs 2.1 crore weighed on other income.
Rupee-driven margin uplift management called uncontrollable; the 18-19% EBITDA band is the stated floor for reinvestment.
SG&A up Rs 23.8 crore QoQ; sales investment must convert to ACV, as TTM ACV was flat.
Constant-currency organic growth is muted and was about 2% in the period discussed; watch whether it moves to the 3-4% range.
Novigo's Middle East exposure given the geopolitical situation.
Annuity revenue remains small; deal durations are project-based.
